CRITERION-BY-CRITERION.
C1 MET. STRATEGY_REGISTRY (backend/backtest/backtest_engine.py:32) now contains stretch_regime -> _compute_stretch_regime_label, qarp -> _compute_qarp_label, reversion_sigma -> _compute_reversion_sigma_label; all three methods confirmed present on BacktestEngine by live import, not by source scan. test_no_candidate_aliases_an_existing_label_method blocks the "new name re-points at an existing method" shape that meta_label exhibits.
C2 MET, and the fixture is NOT rigged -- this was the highest-risk question and I attacked it three ways. (a) My own measurement harness (not the suite's `_labels`) reproduced the claimed numbers EXACTLY: stretch_regime n=880 {-1:315, 0:304, 1:261} top 35.8%; qarp n=528 {-1:66, 0:244, 1:218} top 46.2%; reversion_sigma n=409 {-1:87, 0:196, 1:126} top 47.9%. (b) RE-SEEDED the fixture at seeds 1, 7, 2026, 999331 and 42: top class stayed 35.8-38.0% (stretch_regime), 49.1-53.6% (qarp), 42.4-48.6% (reversion_sigma) -- never within 40 points of the 95% bar. (c) WIDENED the grid 5x (step=1, 4400 rows): 36.4% / 46.7% / 48.8%. The MIN_LABELLED_ROWS=200 floor correctly prevents the "3 rows trivially pass" shape.
C3 MET. mean_reversion measured on the identical fixture at 880/880 rows labelled, {-1:9, 0:836, 1:35}, top class 95.0% -- exact reproduction. The "~all-neutral" report is confirmed true in substance across every seed I tried (neutral 93.6-95.0%). The recorded mechanism (0-on-no-signal floods the neutral class) is consistent with what I observed: mean_reversion labels every row while reversion_sigma labels 409.
C4 MET. The overlay is on the named candidate stretch_regime (up = k*sigma*stretch + cost, down = k*sigma/stretch + cost). The guard is NOT vacuous: mutant M2 (invert up/down) and mutant M2b (compute stretch, then ignore it) BOTH turned test_stretch_overlay_reduces_buy_signals_as_turbulence_rises red. Beyond the test, I verified the overlay end-to-end with the UNPATCHED production _market_stretch: it varies 0.763-2.490 (p25 0.970, median 1.085, p75 1.426; 37.5% of dates above 1.2) on the committed fixture, and the +1 rate falls 40.3% (calmest third, n=290) -> 17.0% (most turbulent third, n=300). The exposure change is real, large, and not an artifact of the injected constants.

FORWARD-LOOKING (the 82.16 concern), verified with MY mutation shape, not the author's. Instead of the suite's 0.5x collapse I replaced the entire post-entry path with a fresh seeded random walk: stretch_regime 563/880 rows changed, qarp 297/880, reversion_sigma 226/880 -> all three carry forward information. quality_momentum 0/880 and factor_model 0/880 -> confirmed NOT forward-looking, reproducing the 82.16 defect by execution. triple_barrier and meta_label raised AttributeError ('BacktestEngine' object has no attribute 'tp_pct'), exactly matching the "stub lacks tp_pct/sl_pct -- not evaluated" caveat disclosed in experiment_results.

MUTATION MATRIX (in-process monkeypatch only; zero repo writes; CONTROL green before and RESTORE-CHECK green after). Killed: M2 invert overlay -> test_stretch_overlay...; M2b overlay inert -> test_stretch_overlay...; M5 reversion_sigma returns 0 instead of None -> test_reversion_sigma_fixes_the_degeneracy_it_replaces. Survived: M1, M3, M4 (see advisories).

ADVISORY FINDINGS -- none blocking, each with a named fix.
A1 (strongest) SURVIVING MUTANT M1: replacing the body of _market_stretch with a constant 1.0 while KEEPING the price fetch leaves all 18 tests GREEN. test_stretch_overlay... patches _market_stretch out entirely, and test_market_stretch_is_backward_looking_only only inspects the requested end date, so neither can observe a flattened regime proxy. The behaviour is correct TODAY -- I measured it end-to-end above -- so this is a future-regression coverage gap, not a criterion miss, and the criterion's guard is genuinely behavioral (two mutants killed it). Fix: add one assertion using the UNPATCHED method, e.g. that _market_stretch spans a spread over F.entry_dates() (observed max/min = 2.490/0.763 = 3.3x) or that the calm-third vs turbulent-third +1-rate gap survives without patching.
A2 SURVIVING MUTANT M3: zeroing the round-trip cost adjustment in _sigma_barriers leaves all 18 green. Cost-adjustment IS implemented (2 * transaction_cost_pct / 100 = 20bps round trip, clearing the >=10bps reality-gap bar) and is claimed prominently in prose and docstrings, but no test guards it.
A3 SURVIVING MUTANT M4: making _compute_qarp_label return 0 instead of None for non-candidates leaves all 18 green (the distribution becomes 880 rows at 67.7% top class, still under the 95% bar). The None-on-no-signal property is guarded for reversion_sigma (M5 killed) but not for qarp.
A4 KNIFE-EDGE ASSERTION: test_existing_mean_reversion_degeneracy_is_measured asserts `top >= MAX_CLASS_SHARE` and passes on an EXACT tie -- 836/880 evaluates to precisely 0.95 in floating point. On all 5 alternate seeds the value is 93.6-94.6%, so this assertion would go red if the fixture is ever regenerated. The companion assertion (neutral >= 0.90) is robust. experiment_results does honestly disclose "exactly at the degeneracy boundary". Fix: relax to >= 0.90, or pin the strict form to the committed seed.
A5 MIRROR DRIFT: IMPLEMENTED_STRATEGY_IDS (backend/meta_evolution/archetype_library.py:31), documented as a "mirror of STRATEGY_REGISTRY", is a hand-maintained frozenset and now diverges by 3 (qarp, reversion_sigma, stretch_regime absent). Drift pre-dates this step ('blend' is in the mirror but not the registry). No behaviour change here -- the validator only fires for archetypes declaring is_implemented=True -- but a future archetype naming one of these candidates would raise spuriously. Per the standing "queue discovered defects" rule this deserves its own step; the durable fix is to DERIVE the mirror from the registry rather than restate it.
